title: Agent Reasoning Failure Modes
description: A diagnostic taxonomy of LLM-agent reasoning failures. Each colloquial label is mapped to its established cognitive-science / AI concept, the way it shows up in practice, and a concrete fix. Organized by the pipeline stage where the failure strikes.

stages.name: Framing
stages.question: Did it solve the right problem?

failure_modes.label: Literalism
failure_modes.tell: Obeys the words, misses the intent.
failure_modes.detail: Executes the literal request even when context makes the real goal obvious. The monkey's-paw / Goodhart problem: the letter of the instruction wins over its purpose.
failure_modes.mitigation: Before acting, paraphrase the underlying goal and check it against the literal wording; when they diverge, surface the intent or ask rather than executing the words verbatim.
failure_modes.citation: Krakovna, V. et al. (2020). Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity. DeepMind. Underlying principle: Goodhart, C. A. E. (1975).
failure_modes.reframe: State the outcome the user actually wants — independent of how they phrased it — before acting on the literal words.

failure_modes.label: Shape of the Example
failure_modes.tell: Copies the example's form, not your goal.
failure_modes.detail: Mirrors the structure, length, or domain of a sample you provided instead of generalizing the task it was meant to illustrate.
failure_modes.mitigation: Separate 'what the example demonstrates' from 'what is being asked,' then solve the underlying task — treat examples as format hints, not as the spec.
failure_modes.citation: Brown, T. B. et al. (2020). Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. NeurIPS 33. arXiv:2005.14165.
failure_modes.reframe: Treat the example as a format hint. Name the underlying task in your own words, then solve that, not the sample's surface form.

failure_modes.label: Shape of the Conversation
failure_modes.tell: Follows the chat's drift over the facts.
failure_modes.detail: Lets how the dialogue was framed — or earlier agreement — steer the answer, echoing the user's premise rather than testing it.
failure_modes.mitigation: Re-ground in the original source facts rather than the conversation's momentum; state disagreement plainly when the evidence contradicts the framing.
failure_modes.citation: Tversky, A. & Kahneman, D. (1981). The framing of decisions and the psychology of choice. Science, 211(4481), 453–458. Sycophancy: Sharma, M. et al. (2023). Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models. arXiv:2310.13548 (Anthropic).
failure_modes.reframe: Re-anchor to the source facts. If this answer would change had the conversation been framed differently, you're echoing, not reasoning.

failure_modes.label: No Questions Asked
failure_modes.tell: Guesses on ambiguity instead of asking.
failure_modes.fix: Ask one clarifying question before guessing.
failure_modes.detail: Faces an ambiguous, load-bearing requirement and silently picks an interpretation instead of surfacing the ambiguity. The complement of Literalism: under-asking rather than over-obeying.
failure_modes.mitigation: When a load-bearing requirement is ambiguous, ask a single targeted question before proceeding rather than committing to a guess.
failure_modes.citation: Cemri, M. et al. (2025). MAST — “Fail to Ask for Clarification”. arXiv:2503.13657.
failure_modes.reframe: If a load-bearing requirement is ambiguous, ask one targeted question before proceeding — don't guess silently.

failure_modes.label: Manufactured Decision
failure_modes.tell: Asks permission for work already authorized.
failure_modes.fix: Already authorized? Act — don't invent a gate.
failure_modes.detail: Appends a confirmation step to work the owner has already approved, converting granted authority back into an owner decision. Performs diligence while handing the task upward. The inverse of No Questions Asked — over-asking rather than under-asking — and distinct from a genuine fork, where the answer would change what gets done.
failure_modes.mitigation: Before asking, check whether authority for this action was already granted; treat a standing authorization as still standing, and reserve questions for forks where the answer changes the next action.
failure_modes.citation: Upward ('reverse') delegation: Oncken, W. Jr. & Wass, D. L. Management Time: Who's Got the Monkey? Harvard Business Review (orig. 1974; reprinted Nov–Dec 1999). The agent-specific form is discussed as 'approval fatigue' / 'confirmation fatigue' in practitioner writing on human-in-the-loop agent governance; NO PEER-REVIEWED SOURCE LOCATED for the agent form — citation deliberately marked incomplete rather than filled with a plausible one.
failure_modes.reframe: Check whether this was already authorized. If it was, act — don't manufacture a decision the owner already made.

stages.name: Reasoning
stages.question: Did it reason about it correctly?

failure_modes.label: Shape of the Data
failure_modes.tell: Treats available data as the whole picture.
failure_modes.detail: Reasons only over what's in hand and assumes nothing important is missing — looking under the streetlight because that's where the light is.
failure_modes.mitigation: Ask 'what data would I need but don't have?' and check for selection or survivorship effects before drawing conclusions from the available set.
failure_modes.citation: Kahneman, D. (2011). Thinking, Fast and Slow (WYSIATI). Survivorship bias: A. Wald (WWII aircraft-survivability analysis). “Streetlight effect” parable.
failure_modes.reframe: Ask what data you'd need but don't have. Don't treat what's in front of you as the whole picture.

failure_modes.label: Shape of the Tool
failure_modes.tell: Lets its tools pick the approach.
failure_modes.detail: Frames the task around the actions it can easily take, not the action the problem actually needs. If all it has is a hammer…
failure_modes.mitigation: Decide the right approach independent of available tools first, then map it to tools; flag when the needed action isn't supported instead of forcing a fit.
failure_modes.citation: Kaplan, A. (1964). The Conduct of Inquiry (law of the instrument). Maslow, A. H. (1966). The Psychology of Science (hammer/nail). Software form: the “golden hammer” anti-pattern.
failure_modes.reframe: Decide the right approach first, ignoring your tools. Then map to tools — and flag if none fit.

failure_modes.label: Shape of the Prior
failure_modes.tell: The default answer beats the evidence given.
failure_modes.detail: Falls back on the common or expected answer from training instead of the specific facts placed in front of it.
failure_modes.mitigation: When provided facts conflict with the 'expected' answer, defer to the in-context evidence and cite the specific source it came from.
failure_modes.citation: Tversky, A. & Kahneman, D. (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science, 185(4157), 1124–1131.
failure_modes.reframe: The specific facts given override your default answer. Cite the in-context evidence, not the common case.

failure_modes.label: First Suspect
failure_modes.tell: Locks on hypothesis #1, skips the rest.
failure_modes.detail: Commits to the first plausible explanation and stops generating alternatives — the classic diagnostic error of closing the search too early.
failure_modes.mitigation: Generate at least two or three alternative explanations before committing, and actively look for evidence that would falsify the leading one.
failure_modes.citation: Croskerry, P. (2003). The Importance of Cognitive Errors in Diagnosis and Strategies to Minimize Them. Academic Medicine, 78(8), 775–780.
failure_modes.reframe: Generate at least two more hypotheses before committing, and name what would disprove your leading one.

failure_modes.label: Sunk Path
failure_modes.tell: Won't abandon a failing approach.
failure_modes.detail: Keeps pushing a chosen plan because it's already invested effort, instead of backtracking. Plan-continuation bias — 'get-there-itis.'
failure_modes.mitigation: Add checkpoints that judge the plan on its remaining merit, ignoring effort already spent, and make backtracking an explicitly allowed move.
failure_modes.citation: Arkes, H. R. & Blumer, C. (1985). The psychology of sunk cost. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 35(1), 124–140. Escalation: Staw, B. M. (1976). Knee-Deep in the Big Muddy. Organizational Behavior and Human Performance, 16(1), 27–44.
failure_modes.reframe: Ignore effort already spent. Judge this approach only on its remaining cost to succeed. Backtracking is allowed.
failure_modes.disambiguator: The objective and constraints are intact and the actions vary, but a plan already shown to be failing is retained across them. If the actions are near-identical, this is D1.

failure_modes.label: Forced Symmetry
failure_modes.tell: Invents parallelism that isn't there.
failure_modes.detail: Treats two sides as equal, or forces a clean symmetric structure onto lopsided reality, because the tidy shape feels right.
failure_modes.mitigation: Weigh positions by evidence quality, not by a need for balance; allow the conclusion to be lopsided when the evidence is lopsided.
failure_modes.citation: Boykoff, M. T. & Boykoff, J. M. (2004). Balance as bias: global warming and the US prestige press. Global Environmental Change, 14(2), 125–136.
failure_modes.reframe: Weigh by evidence, not balance. If the evidence is lopsided, let the conclusion be lopsided.

failure_modes.label: Premature Abstraction
failure_modes.tell: Builds the framework too early.
failure_modes.detail: Generalizes into rules or abstractions before it has enough concrete grounding to know whether they hold.
failure_modes.mitigation: Stay concrete and work through several specific cases first; only generalize once multiple instances support the same rule.
failure_modes.citation: Knuth, D. E. (1974). Structured Programming with go to Statements. ACM Computing Surveys, 6(4), 261–301. Reasoning form: the classical hasty-generalization fallacy.
failure_modes.reframe: Stay concrete. Work several specific cases before proposing any rule or framework.

failure_modes.label: Confabulation
failure_modes.tell: Invents specifics to complete the pattern.
failure_modes.fix: If you don't have the fact, say so — don't invent it.
failure_modes.detail: Fills gaps with plausible-sounding but fabricated specifics — citations, API names, figures — because the pattern 'wants' a value there.
failure_modes.mitigation: Distinguish known facts from generated ones; when a specific (citation, identifier, figure) isn't grounded, flag uncertainty instead of fabricating.
failure_modes.citation: Ji, Z. et al. (2023). Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation. ACM Computing Surveys, 55(12).
failure_modes.reframe: If you don't have a specific fact (citation, API, number), say so. Never invent specifics to complete the pattern.

failure_modes.label: Unchecked Premise
failure_modes.tell: Never tests the starting assumption.
failure_modes.detail: Accepts a premise baked into the request — even a false one — and builds on it without pausing to validate.
failure_modes.mitigation: List the assumptions the task rests on and test the load-bearing ones — including premises embedded in the request itself — before building on them.
failure_modes.citation: Unverified-premise / false-premise (classical logic). LLM acceptance of false premises: Sharma, M. et al. (2023). Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models. arXiv:2310.13548.
failure_modes.reframe: List the assumptions this rests on and test the load-bearing ones — including any premise baked into the request.

failure_modes.label: Sailing
failure_modes.tell: Glides to the end, never checks.
failure_modes.detail: Runs straight through to an answer with no self-check step at all — smooth sailing, right past every place it should have stopped.
failure_modes.mitigation: Insert a mandatory verification step before returning a result: re-run, test, or re-derive the answer rather than trusting the first pass.
failure_modes.citation: Cemri, M. et al. (2025). Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST) — “No or Incomplete Verification”. arXiv:2503.13657.
failure_modes.reframe: Before returning, run an explicit check: re-derive, test, or verify. Do not finish on the first pass alone.
failure_modes.disambiguator: No verification act appears anywhere in the trace, and the agent does not claim one occurred. If a check was attempted, however shallow, this is not C2; if none occurred but one was asserted, this is C7.

failure_modes.label: Skating
failure_modes.tell: Checks the surface only.
failure_modes.detail: Performs a cursory pass that looks like verification but never probes the spots where the result would actually break.
failure_modes.mitigation: Aim verification at the failure-prone parts — edge cases, boundaries, the hardest step — not the parts that are easiest to confirm.
failure_modes.citation: Cemri, M. et al. (2025). MAST — “Incorrect Verification”. arXiv:2503.13657.
failure_modes.reframe: Aim your check at where this would actually break — edge cases, boundaries, the hard step — not the easy parts.
failure_modes.disambiguator: A verification act appears but never executes the artifact under test — it inspects, describes, or reasons about it instead. If the artifact was actually run, this is not C3.

failure_modes.label: Spot-Check
failure_modes.tell: Tests one case, assumes the rest.
failure_modes.detail: Verifies a single example and generalizes 'it works' to all cases, missing the ones that don't.
failure_modes.mitigation: Test multiple cases, including edge and adversarial ones, rather than extrapolating correctness from a single success.
failure_modes.citation: Hasty generalization / sampling fallacy (classical induction).
failure_modes.reframe: Test multiple cases, including adversarial ones. Don't generalize correctness from a single success.
failure_modes.disambiguator: The artifact is executed, but on exactly one case. If coverage extends past a single case, this is not C4.

failure_modes.label: Closure Performance
failure_modes.tell: Looks done; isn't verified.
failure_modes.detail: Delivers a polished, confident 'finished' signal that performs done-ness — the well-formatted answer that's wrong but reads as complete.
failure_modes.mitigation: Gate completion on evidence of correctness, not on a confident-looking output; treat 'finished' and 'verified' as two separate bars to clear.
failure_modes.citation: Cemri, M. et al. (2025). MAST — “Premature Termination”; plus the overconfidence/calibration literature. arXiv:2503.13657.
failure_modes.reframe: Separate 'finished' from 'verified.' Show the evidence that it's correct before declaring done.
failure_modes.disambiguator: Verification happened and covered more than one case, yet completeness is asserted beyond what those checks establish. Use only once C2, C3 and C4 have each been ruled out.

failure_modes.label: Gaming the Check
failure_modes.tell: Makes the check pass dishonestly.
failure_modes.fix: Satisfy the goal, not the gate.
failure_modes.detail: Forces verification green by editing or deleting failing tests, hardcoding expected outputs, or matching the metric rather than the intent. Distinct from Closure Performance, which only looks done — this forces the gate.
failure_modes.mitigation: Treat the check as a proxy for the goal, not the goal itself; never modify, weaken, or special-case the test to pass it.
failure_modes.citation: Reward hacking / specification gaming: Krakovna, V. et al. (2020), DeepMind; Goodhart's law (1975).
failure_modes.reframe: Satisfy the goal, not the gate. Never weaken, edit, or bypass the check to make it pass.

failure_modes.label: Process Misreport
failure_modes.tell: Reports doing work the trace does not contain.
failure_modes.detail: The agent's account of its own process diverges from what the trace shows it did. Two forms: it asserts a check that has no corresponding action ('I ran the tests and they pass', 'I verified this against the source'), or it reports full coverage of work it only partly did (processed the first N inputs under budget pressure and summarised as though all were covered). Distinct from a wrong answer: the object of the falsehood is the agent's own process, not the subject matter.
failure_modes.mitigation: Compare every claimed action against the trace: an assertion about work performed should have a matching tool event. Where coverage was reduced, state the reduction and its cause at the point of reporting, not only on request.
failure_modes.source: No established term is claimed for this mode.
failure_modes.citation: Deliberately unsourced. The nearest published constructs are MAST FM-3.2 'No or incomplete verification' (Cemri et al. 2025), which is about the check being absent rather than about claiming it occurred, and unfaithful chain-of-thought (Turpin et al. 2023), which concerns whether stated reasons drive a prediction rather than honest reporting of a past action. Neither covers this mode; inventing an attribution would be worse than leaving it open.
failure_modes.reframe: Claim only actions that appear in your own trace. If you did not run the check, say you did not run it; if you covered part of the input, say which part and why.
failure_modes.disambiguator: A verification act is absent from the trace AND the agent asserts one occurred, or work was partially covered AND reported as complete. Ask this before C2: if no check occurred and none was claimed, it is C2, not C7.

stages.name: Execution
stages.question: Did it hold the thread across steps?

failure_modes.label: Spinning
failure_modes.tell: Repeats a step with no progress.
failure_modes.fix: No new progress? Change approach, don't repeat.
failure_modes.detail: Re-executes the same or near-identical action across steps without advancing state toward the goal.
failure_modes.mitigation: Detect non-progress (state unchanged across steps) and force an approach change or escalation rather than repeating.
failure_modes.citation: Cemri, M. et al. (2025). MAST — “Step Repetition”. arXiv:2503.13657.
failure_modes.reframe: If the last step produced no new progress, stop and change approach — don't repeat it.
failure_modes.disambiguator: The objective and constraints are intact and the action is near-identical across steps — repetition without progress. If the actions vary, this is B5.

failure_modes.label: Drift
failure_modes.tell: Goal erodes across a long run.
failure_modes.fix: Re-state the goal; cut off-objective work.
failure_modes.detail: Over a long trajectory the working objective gradually diverges from the original task as local sub-goals accumulate.
failure_modes.mitigation: Periodically re-anchor to the original objective and prune actions that no longer serve it.
failure_modes.citation: Goal drift in long-horizon agents; related to MAST trajectory failures (Cemri et al. 2025).
failure_modes.reframe: Restate the original goal and check your current action against it. Cut anything that's wandered off-objective.
failure_modes.disambiguator: The original objective is no longer what is being pursued — a self-generated sub-goal has displaced it. Ask this first: if the objective is still intact, the failure is one of D3, D1 or B5, not D2.

failure_modes.label: Context Bleed
failure_modes.concept: Context loss · lost in the middle
failure_modes.tell: Drops earlier or mid-context constraints.
failure_modes.fix: Re-read the original constraints before acting.
failure_modes.detail: Loses requirements stated earlier or buried mid-context, where models attend least reliably.
failure_modes.mitigation: Re-surface the full constraint set before key steps; don't rely on long-context recall for load-bearing requirements.
failure_modes.citation: Liu, N. F. et al. (2023). Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts. arXiv:2307.03172 (TACL 2024).
failure_modes.reframe: Re-read the original constraints before acting. Confirm you haven't dropped requirements stated earlier or mid-context.
failure_modes.disambiguator: The objective is still being pursued, but a constraint stated earlier in the context is violated. If the objective itself was displaced, this is D2.

failure_modes.label: Say-Do Gap
failure_modes.tell: Reasoning says one thing; the action does another.
failure_modes.fix: Make the action match the stated reasoning.
failure_modes.detail: The narrated reasoning and the executed action diverge — the chain-of-thought doesn't actually drive the behavior.
failure_modes.mitigation: Check that each action follows from the stated reasoning; reconcile divergences before proceeding.
failure_modes.citation: Turpin, M. et al. (2023). Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in CoT Prompting. NeurIPS. MAST: reasoning–action mismatch (Cemri et al. 2025).
failure_modes.reframe: Make your action match your stated reasoning. If they diverge, reconcile them before proceeding.

telemetry.description: Event spec for recording failure-mode detections so they can be counted, correlated, and analyzed over time.

event_schema.run_id: string — groups all events in one agent run/session
event_schema.mode_code: string — e.g. 'B4' (FK to a failure mode)
event_schema.trace_excerpt: string — the snippet that triggered detection

context_tags.task_type: coding | research | data-analysis | writing | planning | tool-use

detector.signal: committed to first cause; no alternatives generated

example_event.trace_excerpt: The error must be the auth token. Fixing that now.

intervention.reframe_text: Generate at least two more hypotheses before committing, and name what would disprove your leading one.

outcome.note: generated 3 hypotheses; real cause was clock skew

analyses_enabled: Frequency — count per mode, sliced by stage / task_type / model.
Co-occurrence — which modes chain within a run (e.g. First Suspect → Sunk Path; Closure Performance masking Sailing/Skating).
Intervention efficacy — resolved-rate per reframe; preflight vs. dynamic-monitor comparison.
Trend — failure rate over time or across model versions.
Hotspots — stage/tag combinations with the highest failure density.

locus.description: What pulls the agent off course.

temporal.description: Whether the failure only appears over multiple steps.

detectability.description: Whether a trace-only critic can catch it, or it needs an external oracle.

family.description: Nearest cognitive-mechanism analog (some trajectory modes are process-native).

chaining.description: Each mode's `pairs_with` lists modes it tends to trigger or mask (directional). Seeds the cross-link UI and the co-occurrence analytics.
chaining.note: Proposed hypotheses — refine against real event-log co-occurrence once data accrues.

field_notes.disambiguator: Present only on modes belonging to a confusable cluster, where the `tell` alone does not separate them. It states a trace-observable test that rules the mode IN or OUT relative to its neighbours. Absence of the field means the mode's `tell` is considered sufficient on its own. Apply the cluster's disambiguators in code order and record which one fired, not only the final code. Cluster lists are given in the order the tests should be applied, which is not always code order: for the trajectory cluster, rule out objective displacement before anything else.
